Bubble wrap was invented to be wallpaper.
In 1957, two engineers in New Jersey, Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes, sealed two shower curtains together, trapping little air bubbles inside.
They thought it would make cool, modern, textured wallpaper.
So they tried selling it as insulation for greenhouses. That didn't really work either.
Then, in 1960, IBM needed a way to protect its new computers during shipping.
The failed wallpaper became one of the most popular packing materials on Earth.
And the most satisfying thing to pop.
